$m^d$ runs for $m$ values in $d$ dimensions; each axis has only $m$ distinct values.

front: Why random search beats grid search
back: When few hyper-parameters matter, $n$ random trials give $n$ distinct values of each, a grid only $n^{1/d}$.

front: Which scale for a learning rate or $\lambda$?
back: A log scale: sample the exponent uniformly.
Evaluate many configurations on a small budget, keep the best $1/\eta$, multiply the budget by $\eta$, repeat. Cheap elimination of bad runs.
Slow starters (e.g. small learning rate) are dropped early; Hyperband hedges with several schedules.
Inner loop tunes hyper-parameters, outer loop estimates performance; avoids the optimism of reporting the best tuning score.
Fit a surrogate to past evaluations, maximise an acquisition function, evaluate there, update.
$k(x,x')=\sigma^2\exp(-(x-x')^2/(2\ell^2))$: length scale $\ell$ sets how far correlation reaches.
$\mu=\mathbf k_*^\top C^{-1}\mathbf t$, $s^2=k_{**}-\mathbf k_*^\top C^{-1}\mathbf k_*$, with $C=K+\beta^{-1}I$.
Cholesky $C=LL^\top$; solve for $\boldsymbol\alpha$; $\mathbf v=L^{-1}\mathbf k_*$; variance $=\sigma^2-\|\mathbf v\|^2$. Cost $O(N^3)$.
Transformers: fit/transform. Model: fit/predict. pipeline.fit fits each step in order; predict only transforms.
Scaling, imputing, feature selection or encoding fitted on all rows lets validation rows influence training; fit inside each fold.

front: Why is the final test set still needed?
back: Trying many configurations overfits the validation score; an untouched test set gives an unbiased estimate.
